summary: Built in 1920 as the Wind-beam Lookout, moved twice, rebuilt at Ramapo Mountain from 1983, and out of service with electrical issues in 2025.

facts.design: Aermotor tower with a 7'x7' cab (NHLR: LS-40; Pierson Ridge record: 60 ft LS-42)
facts.status_note: Out of service in the 2025 season with electrical issues; plans were in the works to staff it for the 2026 fire season

events.note: Erected on Windbeam Mountain as the Wind-beam Lookout with Ringwood Company funds; operated by Section 2 personnel
Moved from Windbeam Mountain. Windbeam record: removed in 1971 and to Pierson Ridge circa 1971. Pierson Ridge record: relocated to Ringwood State Park in 1971
Reached Ramapo Mountain State Forest and has been at its present location since 1983. Pierson Ridge record says the remains were rebuilt there beginning in 1983
Registered on the National Historic Lookout Register as US 45, NJ 2 on July 2, 1992
NHLR visit report dated May 1, 2007 marks the tower as staffed
Out of service with electrical issues during the 2025 season; plans to staff it for the 2026 fire season

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Kept 15 m (50 ft) from Wikipedia's table. The Pierson Ridge record gives 60 ft for an LS-42 and NHLR gives an LS-40 model with no height, so the 60 ft figure is not used.

notes_for_editor: The two Former Fire Lookout Sites records (Windbeam and Pierson Ridge) describe the same tower differently: Windbeam says it went to Pierson Ridge circa 1971 and to Ramapo in 1983; Pierson Ridge says it went to Ringwood State Park in 1971, was later destroyed by vandals, and was rebuilt at Ramapo from 1983. NHLR says moved twice and in place since 1983 without naming the intermediate site. Model (LS-40 vs LS-42) and height (50 ft vs 60 ft) are unresolved. No source found on notable fires, the staffing history before 2007, or whether the tower is open to climbing, so access is omitted. The 2007 visit report is the only staffing observation on NHLR. The 2025 FFLA report is the most recent record and says the tower was out of service that season; it does not say whether the tower was restored in 2026. Fetching the NJ DEP fire-towers page returned no text. The Windbeam page's 1923 newspaper quote (easternuslookouts.weebly.com) was not used.
